title: Protein Interaction Analysis of KaiC3 with Various Kai Homologs via Yeast Two-Hybrid Experiments
author: Anika Wiegard
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.v7ve9n6

steps.title: Prepare Growth Media and Reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary agar and buffer solutions for yeast selection and assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare CSM -Leu -Trp agar (complete supplement mixture lacking leucine and tryptophan).
Prepare Z-Buffer X-Gal solution.

steps.title: Transform Yeast Cells
steps.instruction: Transform yeast cells and select for successful transformants.

substeps.instruction: Perform transformation using the Frozen-EZ Yeast Transformation II Kit (Zymo Research) according to manufacturer's guidelines.
Select transformed cells on CSM -Leu -Trp agar at 30 °C for 3–4 days.

steps.title: Prepare Master Plate
steps.instruction: Spot colonies onto a second selection plate for further analysis.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend 3 colonies in 100 µl H2O.
Spot 5 µl of the suspension onto a second CSM -Leu -Trp plate.
Wrap the plate in parafilm.
Incubate at 30 °C for 2 days.

steps.title: Prepare Z-Buffer/X-Gal Filter Stack
steps.instruction: Prepare pre-soaked filters for the β-galactosidase activity assay.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 5 ml of Z-Buffer/X-Gal solution for each 10 cm circular plate by mixing 10 ml Z-Buffer, 27 µl β-Mercaptoethanol, and 42 µl X-Gal solution.
Stack 3 sterile filters in a petri-dish and add 5 ml of the Z-buffer/X-Gal solution.
Store the pre-soaked filters in a plastic bag to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Transfer Colonies to Filter
steps.instruction: Transfer yeast colonies from the agar plate to a sterile filter.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a petri-dish with 1 sterile dry filter and mark the orientation (e.g., top with a pencil line).
Using tweezers, place the dry filter in the correct orientation onto the colony plate.
Gently rub the filter with a sterile glass spreader until the filter becomes wet and spots are visible for all colonies.

steps.title: Freeze-Thaw Treatment
steps.instruction: Subject the colony-laden filter to repeated freeze-thaw cycles to permeabilize cells.

substeps.instruction: Lift the filter off the agar plate and submerge it in liquid nitrogen for approximately 10 s.
Once completely frozen, place the filter back into the petri dish (colonies facing up) and let it thaw at room temperature (RT).
Repeat the freezing and defrosting process 3-5 times.

steps.title: Incubate for Color Development
steps.instruction: Incubate the treated filter on the pre-soaked stack to detect protein interactions.

substeps.instruction: Remove excess liquid from the pre-soaked 3-filter stack.
Place the colony-laden filter (colony side up) on top of the pre-soaked stack, ensuring no air bubbles are trapped between filters.
Store the plates in a plastic bag and incubate at RT, preferably in the dark due to X-Gal light sensitivity.
Check periodically for the appearance of blue colonies.

steps.title: Stop Reaction and Record Results
steps.instruction: Terminate the assay and document the findings.

substeps.instruction: Remove the filter from the pre-soaked stack and let it dry open under a fume hood.
Scan the plates to record results.
Identify positive protein interactions by the presence of a blue color change in the colony compared to controls.
